mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is persistently below its long-run average for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days tends to be positive due to lower real borrowing costs and increased equity discounting.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < avg(FEDFUNDS) over the past 12 months
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window following the trigger, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the 30-day rolling mean (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in consumer pay growth (PAYEMS vs. HOUST) predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days as labor market weakness dampens business optimism.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 10% month-over-month while HOUST decreases by > 5% month-over-month
failure_condition: In 70% of similar triggered events, the 20-day forward return is non-negative (quantile regression slope < 0).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) grows faster than consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL), it signals a shift toward supply-side demand expansion, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO growth rate > CPIAUCSL growth rate over the prior month
failure_condition: In 50+ such triggered windows, the 5-day forward return is negative or flat (median < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive month of contracting retail sales (not directly observable in the given proxies; use proxy for demand such as HOUST) combined with rising industrial production (INDPRO) predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days due to supply-chain stress and profit compression.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases for two consecutive months while INDPRO increases by > 2% month-over-month
failure_condition: Across 10 analogous events, the 20-day forward return is positive or at least not statistically different from zero (Granger causality rejected).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 5% for three consecutive months is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days as higher labor market friction reduces growth expectations.
failure_condition: In 40 such episodes, the 60-day forward return is non-negative (median > 0).

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) accelerates faster than wage growth (HOUST), it indicates cost pressures that suppress corporate profit margins and drive negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL growth rate > HOUST growth rate over the prior 2 months
failure_condition: In 30 such triggered windows, the 20-day forward return is positive or at least not significantly different from zero (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in retail activity (proxy via HOUST) for four consecutive months, despite stable industrial production (INDPRO), predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days due to recessionary demand signals.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases for four consecutive months while INDPRO remains flat or increases modestly (< 1% mmo)
failure_condition: In 20 such events, the 5-day forward return is positive (median > 0).

mechanism_narrative: During a sharp rise in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 3% for two consecutive months without a corresponding increase in pay growth (PAYEMS), the S&P 500 is expected to deliver negative forward returns over the next 20 days as the Fed is likely to tighten policy soon.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 3% for two consecutive months and PAYEMS growth rate < CPIAUCSL growth rate
failure_condition: In 40 such triggered windows, the 20-day forward return is non-negative (median ≥ 0).
